The study described is experiencing **lead-time bias**. If the survival rate is measured from the date of diagnosis, the screened group will appear to have a better 5-year survival rate simply because they were identified earlier in the disease progression, not because the treatment or detection improved the outcome. To determine the change in resistance to blood flow, we use Poiseuille's Law, which states that resistance ($R$) is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the radius ($r$) of the vessel: $R \propto 1/r^4$. $R_{new} \propto 1/(0.5 \cdot r_{old})^4$
$R_{new} \propto 1/(0.0625 \cdot r_{old}^4)$
$R_{new} = R_{old} / 0.0625 = 16 \cdot R_{old}$
